st: Cut the flank steak into 3 or 4 large chunks and place them in a large pot with the broth, 1 bay leaf and [[1 tsp]] of the salt.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the beef is very tender and pulls apart easily.
Lift the beef out onto a plate and save the broth. Let the beef cool for 10 minutes, then shred it into thin strands with two forks.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper for [[8 minutes]] until soft.
Stir in the garlic, [[1 tsp]] cumin and [[1 tsp]] oregano and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomato sauce, the diced tomatoes, [[1 cup]] of the saved broth, the second bay leaf, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the shredded beef and the olives. Simmer uncovered until the sauce clings to the meat and is no longer watery.
Remove the bay leaves, taste, and add salt if needed. Serve hot with white rice and fried plantains.
Slice each piece of bread in half lengthwise like a book, leaving the roll in one piece if possible.
Spread [[1 tbsp]] mustard on the cut side of each sandwich, using [[4 tbsp]] in all.
Layer on 2 slices of Swiss cheese, then the roast pork, then the ham, then 4 pickle chips per sandwich, then 2 more slices of Swiss on top so the cheese melts around the filling.
Close the sandwiches and spread the outsides lightly with the [[3 tbsp]] softened butter.
Heat a large skillet or griddle over medium heat. Place a sandwich in the pan and set a heavy pan or a foil-wrapped brick on top to press it flat.
Cook for [[3 minutes]] per side, pressing down, until the bread is crisp and golden and the cheese has melted.
Slice each sandwich on the diagonal and serve hot.
Soak the beans in plenty of cold water overnight, or cover them with water, boil for 2 minutes, and let sit for 1 hour. Drain.
Put the beans in a pot with [[6 cups]] fresh water and the bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered until just tender.
Meanwhile, cook the bacon in a large heavy pot over medium heat until crisp. Add [[2 tbsp]] olive oil, the onion and the bell pepper and cook for [[6 minutes]].
Add the garlic, [[1 tsp]] cumin and [[1 tsp]] oregano and stir for 1 minute.
Scoop the beans out of their liquid with a slotted spoon into the pot. Measure [[3 cups]] of the bean liquid and add it, along with [[2 tsp]] salt.
Stir in the rice and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover tightly, and cook without lifting the lid.
Turn off the heat and let it rest covered for 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork, remove the bay leaf and serve.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper for [[6 minutes]] until soft.
Add the garlic and stir for 1 minute.
Add the ground beef, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Break the meat up with a spoon and cook until browned and no pink remains, reaching 160°F (71°C).
Stir in [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] oregano and the bay leaf and cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the tomato sauce and add the raisins. Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens and coats the meat.
Stir in the olives, simmer 3 more minutes, remove the bay leaf and serve with white rice.

ing: or 0.5 cup orange juice plus 0.5 cup lime juice
st: Mash the garlic with [[1.5 tbsp]] salt in a bowl until pasty. Stir in the oregano, cumin, pepper, olive oil and the sour orange juice to make the mojo.
Poke the pork all over with a knife tip, about 30 deep slits.
Place the pork in a large dish or bag and pour the mojo over it, working it into the slits. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Spread the onion rings in a roasting pan and set the pork on top with the marinade.
Cover tightly with foil and roast, basting once every hour with the pan juices.
Remove the foil, raise the oven to 400°F (200°C), and roast until the outside is browned and the meat is very tender. Check that it reaches at least 190°F (88°C) for pull-apart texture.
Rest the pork for 20 minutes, then shred or slice and spoon the pan juices and onions over it.

ing: or half orange and half lime juice
st: Cut the peeled cassava into 3-inch chunks, then cut each lengthwise in half and remove the tough woody center cord.
Put the cassava in a pot with [[8 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce to a steady simmer and cook until a fork pierces the pieces easily and they look slightly translucent.
Drain well and keep warm in a serving bowl.
Warm the [[0.33 cup]] olive oil in a small pan over medium-low heat. Add the onion and cook for [[5 minutes]] until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds only, until fragrant, so it does not turn bitter.
Pour in the sour orange juice and [[1 tsp]] salt, bring to a quick simmer, then spoon over the hot cassava and serve.
Cut the ends off each plantain, score the peel lengthwise, and pry it off with your fingers. Slice into 1-inch thick rounds.
Stir the garlic, [[0.5 cup]] warm water, lime juice and [[0.5 tsp]] salt together in a small bowl.
Heat [[2 cups]] oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat to about 325°F (160°C). Fry the rounds in batches for [[3 minutes]] per side until pale golden and soft.
Move the rounds to paper towels. While warm, press each one flat to about 0.25 inch thick with the bottom of a glass or a plate.
Dip each flattened piece briefly in the garlic water, then shake off the excess.
Raise the heat to medium-high, to about 375°F (190°C), and fry the pieces again until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and serve right away.
Place the flank steak in a pot with [[6 cups]] water, the bay leaf, half the onion and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce to a simmer and cook, partly covered, until the beef is tender enough to shred.
Remove the beef and let it cool for 15 minutes. Shred it into thin strands with two forks.
Toss the shredded beef with the lime juice, garlic, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Let it marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Spread the beef in an even layer, working in batches if needed.
Press down and cook without stirring until the underside is browned and crisp, then turn and crisp the other side.
Cook the remaining sliced onion in the same pan for [[4 minutes]] until soft and slightly browned, scatter over the beef and serve with rice and beans.
Soak the beans in cold water overnight, then drain. Or cover with water, boil 2 minutes, and let sit 1 hour before draining.
Put the beans in a large pot with [[8 cups]] fresh water and the bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered.
Meanwhile, heat [[3 tbsp]] olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper for [[8 minutes]] until soft.
Add the garlic, [[2 tsp]] cumin and [[1 tsp]] oregano and stir for 1 minute.
Scrape the skillet mixture into the beans. Add [[2 tsp]] salt and simmer partly covered until the beans are very soft and the broth has thickened.
Remove the bay leaves. Mash about a cup of the beans against the side of the pot, or blend part of the soup, to make it thicker.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] red wine vinegar, taste for salt, and serve over white rice with chopped raw onion if you like.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion for [[2 minutes]] until soft.
Whisk in [[0.5 cup]] flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring, to make a paste.
Slowly pour in the warm milk, whisking constantly, and cook until very thick like a stiff paste.
Stir in the ham, nutmeg and salt. Spread the mixture in a shallow dish, cover the surface with plastic wrap, and chill until firm.
Scoop spoonfuls and roll into cylinders about 2 inches long. Roll each in a little flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C). Fry the croquetas in small batches, turning, until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Unfold the puff pastry on a floured surface and cut each sheet into 4 squares, making 8 in all.
Cut the guava paste into 8 thin rectangles and put one on each square. Spread or dot about [[1.5 tsp]] cream cheese next to it.
Brush the edges with the beaten egg, fold the pastry over into a triangle or rectangle, and press the edges with a fork to seal.
Place on the sheet, brush the tops with egg and sprinkle with the [[2 tbsp]] sugar. Cut a small slit in each top.
Bake until puffed and deep golden brown.
Cool on a rack for 10 minutes before serving, since the filling is very hot.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Have a 9-inch round cake pan or flan mold and a larger roasting pan ready.
Melt the [[1 cup]] sugar in a heavy saucepan over medium heat without stirring until it turns a deep amber color. Swirl the pan gently as it browns.
Carefully pour the caramel into the cake pan and tilt to coat the bottom. It will harden quickly, and it is very hot.
Blend or whisk the eggs, condensed milk, evaporated milk, vanilla and salt until smooth. Strain through a sieve to remove lumps.
Pour the custard over the caramel. Cover the pan tightly with foil.
Set the pan inside the roasting pan and pour hot water around it to come halfway up the sides. Bake until the center is just set and slightly jiggly.
Cool to room temperature, then chill in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours.
Run a knife around the edge, set a plate on top, and flip to unmold so the caramel sauce pours over the flan.

ing: optional, use extra soda water for a virgin version
st: Put the mint leaves, the lime wedges and the [[2 tsp]] sugar in a sturdy glass.
Gently muddle with a spoon handle, pressing just enough to release the lime juice and mint oils without shredding the mint.
Pour in [[2 fl oz]] white rum and stir until the sugar dissolves. Skip the rum for a non-alcoholic mojito.
Fill the glass with the crushed ice.
Top with [[3 fl oz]] cold soda water and stir once from the bottom to mix.
Slap a mint sprig between your hands to wake up its aroma, tuck it in the glass and serve with a straw.
Cook the bacon in a heavy pot over medium heat for 6 minutes until crisp.
Add the onion and pepper and cook 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, [[1 tsp]] cumin and [[1 tsp]] oregano for 1 minute.
Add the rice and stir 1 minute to coat it in the fat.
Pour in the beans with their liquid, plus [[2 cup]] water. Add the bay leaf and [[1.5 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil and cook uncovered until the water drops to the rice level, about 8 minutes.
Stir once, cover, and cook on the lowest heat 20 minutes until the rice is tender and the pot is dry. Rest 5 minutes, then fluff.
nt: Simmered in one pot, then steamed covered
Best swap: use smoked paprika and olive oil in place of the bacon for a vegetarian version.
